title: Push attribution checkpoints to the remote records branch
summary: write_checkpoint in attribution.rs appends only to the local records branch via RecordsWriter::append, so the next write resets it away. Change it to use RecordsWriter::append_to_remote (compare-and-swap, retry) so a passing check's checkpoint reaches the remote and later landings fast-forward past it. Audience: maintainers and CI, whose incremental run should judge only commits after the checkpoint.

defaults_applied.how: New tests plus cargo test, clippy, fmt pass.
Fix the write path so checkpoints are pushed, not the reset symptom.
Tests read the remote branch directly.
Doc comments and changelog written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-gate/src/attribution.rs: write_checkpoint (line ~727) builds a Checkpoint and calls RecordsWriter::append, which writes only the local ref; read_newest_checkpoint (~549) is the reader, and tests passing_check_writes_checkpoint, failing_check_writes_no_checkpoint, checkpoint_write_failure_keeps_verdict and put_checkpoint already exist. Read crates/athena-git/src/records_branch.rs: append_to_remote (~398) syncs from the remote, builds on the remote tip, pushes with push_if_remote_at (expected-tip guard), retries on rejection up to max_attempts, then returns RecordsError::Contended. Resolution order: sync_from(remote), fetch tip, plan, build_commit, push. Records validation: no new record or data file is added; the checkpoint is the existing HistoryRecord::Checkpoint under CHECKPOINT_DIR, already accepted by check_record_file / AnyRecord in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs, and the existing round-trip tests there cover it. The property is measured directly by reading the remote records ref in a test repo after the check, not via the local ref.
Environment: the push goes to the configured git remote's records branch (a local bare repo in tests); write permission to the records branch; reads the remote tip. No CI workflow files change.

The request lists crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs, which does not exist in the repository (no gh* under crates/athena-core/src); it is treated as not needing change, and the remote name is obtained from the existing caller context. If a remote name needs plumbing it goes through attribution.rs.
A failed push stays a reported checkpoint_error and keeps the verdict, as checkpoint_write_failure_keeps_verdict requires.
athena land also writes a checkpoint through the same write_checkpoint path, so one fix covers both; no athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow change is needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-gate/src/attribution.rs, run with `cargo test -p athena-gate`, shows that after a passing check the checkpoint file exists on the remote records branch (read from the bare remote, not the local ref).

A test run by `cargo test -p athena-gate` shows that a later landing/records write after the checkpoint leaves the checkpoint on the remote and the remote tip is a descendant of the checkpoint commit (fast-forward only, no reset).
A test run by `cargo test -p athena-gate` shows an incremental attribution run, starting from the remote checkpoint, judges only commits after its main_sha rather than replaying in full.

A test in crates/athena-git/src/records_branch.rs or attribution.rs shows a checkpoint push that loses a race is retried on the new remote tip and still lands; a persistent push failure keeps the verdict and sets checkpoint_error.
Grep of crates/athena-gate/src/attribution.rs shows write_checkpoint calls append_to_remote rather than append.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing that checkpoints are now pushed to the remote records branch.
cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check all pass.

out_of_scope: Changing the records record schema or adding record files
hard_reason: Changes the records writer path that landing and the history check depend on, so a mistake can silently corrupt or drop records.
